name: Combined Immunodeficiency with Low CD4 and Normal CD8

criteria.description: Persistently low CD4+ T lymphocyte count below age-adjusted normal ranges
Normal or near-normal CD8+ T lymphocyte count
History of recurrent or severe infections typical of T-cell immunodeficiency
Demonstrated impaired lymphocyte proliferation to mitogens or antigens
Exclusion of secondary causes of CD4 lymphopenia such as HIV infection or immunosuppressive therapy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of persistently low CD4+ T cell count with normal CD8+ count, recurrent opportunistic infections, and exclusion of secondary causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may aid in confirming diagnosis but is not always available.

pathognomonic.notes: Including Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia and candidiasis
searchTerms: frequent infections from weak immune system
persistent infections due to immune problems

pathognomonic.notes: Due to chronic infections and malabsorption
searchTerms: failure to gain weight as baby

common.notes: Persistent fungal infections of skin and mucosa
searchTerms: chronic yeast infections on skin and mucous

common.notes: Enlarged lymph nodes due to immune dysregulation
Often related to infections or malabsorption

occasional.notes: Enlargement of liver and spleen due to immune activation
Including autoimmune hemolytic anemia and thrombocytopenia
Painful recurrent ulcers in oral mucosa

rare.notes: Formation of granulomas in various tissues
Increased risk due to immune dysregulation

laboratory: Low absolute CD4+ T cell count with normal CD8+ T cell count
imaging: Chest X-ray showing recurrent pneumonia or bronchiectasis
genetic: Mutations in genes involved in T cell development or signaling (e.g., IL2RG, CD3D) may be identified
other: Exclusion of HIV infection by serology and PCR
Flow cytometry immunophenotyping confirming lymphocyte subsets

distinguishingFeatures: Profound deficiency of both CD4+ and CD8+ T cells
More severe clinical presentation in infancy
Often associated with absent or severely reduced B cell function
Presence of HIV antibodies or RNA
Progressive decline in CD4+ T cells with variable CD8+ counts
History of risk factors for HIV exposure

redFlags: Severe or recurrent opportunistic infections in early childhood
Failure to thrive despite adequate nutrition
Persistent unexplained lymphopenia with low CD4+ count
references: Notarangelo LD. Primary immunodeficiencies. J Allergy Clin Immunol. 2010;125(2 Suppl 2):S182-94.

Orange JS, et al. Use and interpretation of diagnostic vaccination in primary immunodeficiency: a working group report of the AAAAI Primary Immunodeficiency Committee. J Allergy Clin Immunol. 2012;130(3 Suppl):S1-24.
